The fix after the review: the launch keeps the receiver's exit status; for a receiver that exited END_UNRECORDED with its dispatch still running the runner's unknown record has the reason outcome_unknown:end_unrecorded, and outcome_unknown for one it killed or that ended another way; a receiver whose output has ended is given its exit before the kill; invoke sends the receiver's standard error to a file beside the run's execution record, where a receiver that failed writes its error's class, refusal code and status. Fix 2: a receiver that exits END_UNRECORDED before its dispatch's record reaches running is recorded unknown with the reason launch_evidence_missing:end_unrecorded, apart from one that ended there with another status or was killed, which is recorded launch_evidence_missing as before.

suites.name: 151_veldo_0313_space_run
suites.regions: The CLI's space verb and the run wrapper (VELDO-0313, design 3, 6.3, 6.7 and 6.9, and the fix round after its review), in bin/veldo. veldo space run: the run is issued by the authority to space-runner through the issuer the wiring carries, never by the wrapper; its hold is placed and admission asked; its scratch root is declared before it is made, owned by the run with its station, with the run's supervisor as its recorded process; the command is given its temporary folder, its space label and its compose project name. The wrapper returns the command's own status as soon as the command exits, waits for nothing else and stops nothing. When the kernel shows nothing of the run (its supervisor has ended, its containment group was read and is empty, no process in the table carries its label), the census of the run's worktree and of its labelled Docker objects, run finished through Signal and the release of the hold are written in that order, every one as space-runner through the Ledger's own rule. A process the command left, a worker a server outside the command's tree started with the run's label, an orphaned process nobody can read, a group nobody could read and a group that gains a process keep run finished and the release back; the end follows the exit of what held it, woken by that exit. The build folder the command made has an item and goes with the scratch root; untracked notes and a folder only a personal exclude rule covers stay; an item of the run the owner marked Keep and another run's scratch root are not reached; another run's container and one with no label get no item. In act mode with too little space the wrapper prints the numbers, returns 75, starts nothing, makes no folder and releases the hold; in report mode it prints the numbers and starts the command. veldo space record and veldo space event (a host script's forms): an unknown kind or event type, a path outside every known root, a path on the protect list (also through a link) and a path with a .. segment are refused by name with nothing written; the record verb records a worktree or an agent repository before it is made and confirms it after, and refuses the kind scratch, a session as owner and every path that exists, so existing work is never an item that is removed unsaved; the event verb takes released alone and refuses the hooks' types (ref changed, session started, session ended) by name before anything is sent or spooled (design 6.9, the lead's decision at assembly). With no central installation each verb says so and the wrapper runs its command unchanged, as it does for a ledger this process cannot reach, for an installation whose switch is off and for a wiring with no issuer. Fix round 3: a block of the process reader rules no unread process out; the supervisor that stays points its descriptors 0, 1 and 2 at /dev/null first, so a caller that reads the wrapper's output to its end is not held by what the command left; and the supervisor says, from inside its wait, that it is asleep on the exit of what is left. With the reader's label (VELDO-0344): of a reader's block only a label that was read decides; this run's label makes the process a holder, and a label that is not this run's takes it out. Fix round 4 of VELDO-0315: losing the report's reader ends the reporting and never the supervision, a stop sent after the command ended ends nothing, the run of a wrapper that went while its command ran still gets its end, and the supervisor that stays reads the process table again only when every holder the last read named has exited, so it uses no processor while it waits.
